plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the source and measurements support three complementary opportunities in this one-kernel O(N²) workload—reuse source particles across target rows, increase parallelism within each target row, and reduce per-interaction arithmetic. The first two are distinct execution mappings; the third can be tested independently and combined later. The supplied baseline is valid and correct, with three reported search times averaging 0.00185514 s; per-size timings and independent confirmation are not provided, so this is a baseline rather than evidence for any optimization. The target and interface are specified as one GH200, NVRTC CUDA 12.6.3, fixed Particle layout and entry point, and limited launch configuration. CUDA documentation consulted was the publisher-current CUDA Best Practices Guide 13.4, not version-matched to the target; it supports only general memory-hierarchy and floating-point-rounding considerations, not a target-specific performance claim.
